sections.heading: C — Liability insurance proof, REAL ID, moving to North Carolina, renewal and duplicate licenses
sections.markdown:
## C — Liability insurance proof, REAL ID, moving to North Carolina, renewal and duplicate licenses
Knowledge domain: who must prove insurance, what a REAL ID is, deadlines for new residents, and how licenses are renewed, replaced and updated.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
A free identification card is available to applicants who are homeless with a shelter letter, legally blind with a physician letter, or 70 or older with no extra papers needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
A free ID card is also available when your driving record shows a medical cancellation, or when you have a developmental disability documented by a primary care provider's letter. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Some license applicants must show printed proof of automobile liability insurance; a picture of it on a phone is not accepted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Insurance proof is required when applying for an original license, including an out-of-state transfer, when a license is restored after suspension or revocation, and when a court grants a Limited Driving Privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Form DL-123, insurance binders and certificates are only good for 30 days after they are issued. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
An applicant who owns no currently registered vehicle and does not drive someone else's non-fleet private passenger vehicle signs a certification of exemption, Form DL-123A, at the license office. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
That exemption limits the driver to Fleet Vehicles Only, and removing it costs a $16.75 duplicate fee plus proof of financial responsibility. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
To avoid delays, get Form DL-123 from your insurance agent before you go to the license office. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
The REAL ID Act of 2005 raised security standards for state licenses and ID cards, and North Carolina's REAL ID meets federal identification rules for the TSA and federal facilities. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
A REAL ID is a North Carolina license, learner permit or ID card that carries a star. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
REAL ID rules affect domestic commercial air travelers, including unaccompanied minors under 18, and visitors to federal sites that require ID such as military bases, prisons and nuclear plants. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
Without a REAL ID you can still enter those federal sites, but you must bring additional documents, so check with the agency, such as the TSA, before you go. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
Federal law requires every non-REAL ID license or ID card to show the words Not for Federal Identification on its face. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
NCDMV started issuing REAL ID and non-REAL ID cards in May 2017, and a REAL ID costs nothing extra beyond the usual fees. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
A REAL ID requires a visit to a local driver license office, after you first meet every requirement for the license, permit or ID card itself. [A02]
Why it matters: dynamic detail: appointment options and the document list are kept on the DMV and REAL ID websites.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A03
A new resident must get a North Carolina license or learner permit within 60 days of establishing residence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A03
A new resident who wants to keep a commercial license from another jurisdiction must apply for and receive a North Carolina CDL within 30 days of becoming a resident. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A03
For an applicant who has lived in North Carolina less than 12 months, DMV must finish a National Sex Offender Public Registry search before issuing a license or ID card. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
A new resident applying for a Class C license may have to take the knowledge, vision and traffic signs tests, plus a driving test if the examiner thinks it is needed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
A nonresident is someone whose legal residence is in another state, territory or jurisdiction, or in a foreign country. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
Examples of nonresidents include travelers passing through, out-of-state college students who plan to go home, service members stationed in North Carolina who plan to return home, and spouses of nonresident service members. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
North Carolina stores customer photos and signatures digitally, and each license or ID card has a bar code holding customer data. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
Licenses are made at a central location, so after testing and a photo you receive a temporary driving certificate valid for 60 days, and the new card arrives by mail within 60 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
You may keep using your current license or ID card as photo identification until the new one is delivered. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A04
Drivers under 21 get a vertical license or ID card; under 18 it has red and yellow bars marking the 18th and 21st birthdays, and from 18 to 20 one red bar marks the 21st birthday. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A04
About six months before a license expires, DMV mails a reminder card showing how many years the renewal will last, but you can renew without the card. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A04
Renewing at a driver license office requires a vision test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A04
A license may be renewed any time within 180 days before it expires. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A04
If you renew without your current or expired license, you must show the examiner two identification documents. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A04
A resident who has been out of state for at least 30 days in a row may renew by mail, getting a temporary license that ends 60 days after returning to North Carolina or on its printed expiration date, whichever is first. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A04
Renewal by mail requires a verifiable North Carolina residence, a Class C license expired no more than two years, a DMV photo from the last five years, a physician-signed vision statement, a sex offender affidavit, and an age no older than 72. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A04
Renewal by mail is allowed only every other renewal cycle, and commercial and full provisional licenses can never be renewed by mail. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A04
An active-duty service member living outside North Carolina may renew by mail with military orders and a front-and-back copy of the military ID, using a host family address if needed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A05
With papers showing active duty, a military renewal may be done more than a year before expiration, and the DMV photo may be up to eight years old. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A05
A military-designation license may be renewed by mail no more than two times in the holder's lifetime, and military spouses and dependents may also renew by mail. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A05
A military dependent with a full provisional license can upgrade to Class C at age 18 if the license has been expired no more than one year. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A05
A returning service member does not need to visit a license office until the license is due for renewal. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A05
A qualified veteran can add a VETERAN designation by bringing an honorable discharge form such as the DD-214, and it is added at the next renewal at no extra charge. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A06
A veteran who wants the designation before renewal can get it on a duplicate license for the usual duplicate fee. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A06
A license expires on your birthday: one issued at ages 18 through 65 lasts 8 years, and one issued at 66 or older lasts 5 years. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F41 | anchor: A06
To get a duplicate, the license must not be expired, suspended or cancelled; a lost or stolen license can be replaced by showing two DMV-approved identification documents, or online if you know your license number. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F42 | anchor: A06
After an address change you must tell the division within 60 days and get a duplicate license, unless the address changed through government action without you moving. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F43 | anchor: A06
After a name change you must notify the division within 60 days and get a duplicate, and you should update Social Security at least 24 hours before visiting DMV. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F44 | anchor: A06
A name change is proven by a certified marriage certificate, court or Register of Deeds records, or a notarized Form DL-101, issued by an agency of the United States, Puerto Rico, a U.S. territory or Canada. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]

Misconceptions: a phone photo of an insurance card does not count as proof; a non-REAL ID card is still a valid license for driving; renewal by mail is not available for full provisional licenses; the address-change deadline applies even though no new test is needed.
Mnemonics: Star means REAL; the three S changes — Settling in as a new resident, Street address and Surname — all share the same deadline.
Glossary: REAL ID means a federally compliant license or ID marked with a star; financial responsibility means proof of liability insurance; duplicate means a replacement license with the same expiration; nonresident means a person whose legal home is outside North Carolina.
Dynamic facts: fees, appointment options, phone numbers and online-service availability can change and are isolated as dynamic; confirm them on the DMV website.
